subject: pe
title: Media, Money and Match-Fixing
welcome_lead: Broadcasting rights, betting markets, integrity risks — sport's commercial reality.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on media, commercialisation and integrity issues.
final_note: Every revenue stream is also a risk vector — integrity is now sport's most fragile commodity.

concepts.def: Payments by media for exclusive coverage; English Premier League ~$13 bn over 3 yr.
Brand association with athletes/teams for marketing value.
Manipulation of results, often for betting profit.
Manipulation of in-play events (e.g., specific deliveries in cricket).
Internal sport body monitoring betting and match-fixing (e.g., ICC ACU).
Global market ~$70 bn, growing with online platforms.

walkthroughs.body_html: Premier League revenues are over half TV rights. Broadcasting reshapes scheduling and rule changes.
Spot-fixing requires only manipulating brief in-game moments; harder to detect than match-fixing.
WADA-style integrity units, athlete education and bet-monitoring algorithms aim to deter fixers.
